mode: Built-in ImageGen. Art studies assembled in a review-only Godot fixture. No use of game saves.

firstPass.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Generate one isolated isometric in-game treasure sprite on TRUE TRANSPARENT alpha for a mobile Dungeon Empire review. Image 1 is solely palette, light, camera and masonry STYLE reference from the actual game. Image 2 is solely a COIN MATERIAL and coin size reference: nothing from its chest, especially no chest. The entire subject must fit with alpha margin on every side, no background, no room perimeter, no wall, no doors, no chest, no creatures, no HUD, no letters, no text or frame. Orthographic 2:1 isometric projection, viewing the floor from above at 30° elevation. It must read at 150 screen pixels wide. Match the stylized smooth game sprites: cool shadow from deep blue-purple ambient, warmer bronze shadows in the coins, small restrained pale gold glints on top-left edges, simple grouped shapes, clean contours. Each coin is a small flattened ellipse with a dark bronze edge. No giant medallion or neon yellow glow. Render the physical object(s) only; leave the ground transparent and keep shadow restrained. Transparent wide horizontal composition. Direction A, L'Éboulis d'or. A broad, irregular, low island of spilled gold consisting of THREE joined, asymmetrically heaped small piles of coins touching and overlapping to read as ONE central communal hoard. The highest dome is off centre toward the rear-left. A smaller tongue spills toward the lower right, with just a few coins breaking away. Visually think of many hundreds of coins, simplified into larger midtones at game size. Most coins lie loosely in heaps and overlap in different directions; only three or four short coin stacks at most. The top of the pile should be notably lower than a short dungeon wall. Natural draping directly on the stone floor (not depicted), no plinth, no coin press, no stone ring or circular carpet. The ONLY visible material in this prop is gold.

Transparent wide horizontal composition. Direction B, La Fosse de la dîme. A shallow SQUARE masonry-lined coin recess cut flush into a blue slate floor, seen as one clean symmetric 2:1 floor-plane diamond. Centered within the recess are several generous mounds of many tiny gold coins with distinct short orderly stacks along the rear half, all touching as ONE shared gold hoard. The recess is FULL to the rim, small coin heaps rise just a little above floor level. Its lip is only one thin row of bevelled slate capstones matching the reference dungeon's indigo colour, stone size and simple black masonry seams. It is a subtle inward bevel with inside shadow, top surface only, absolutely NO visible outer side walls or pedestal faces and NO deep pit. The volume is carved down, not raised up. Stone top rim edges project as straight parallel isometric axes; tips of the rhombus at left/right aligned horizontally. Keep a little dark slate visible between the stacks, some gold has spilled irregularly up to the lip. No boxes of any kind, no gilded frame, no lid, no jewelry or magical gems, no handlebars. It must look like a flush floor insert that remains legible when set among existing dungeon slabs.

selected.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Reference image 1 is a Godot concept screenshot and is the authoritative surrounding game art and isometric camera. Reference 2 is the existing mobile chest for reference to its tiny coins. Output ONLY a new isolated TRUE transparent painted sprite of the central coin hoard from image 1 for compositing back onto the same game floor. The ONLY requested design change is the unit coin scale and volume from groups of small coins. The previous loose coins are far too large relative to the individual blue paving stones. Replace each coin with groups of at least 5 markedly SMALLER coins in the same area, approximately 30 to 36 coins could fit across the whole prop laid side by side, although most overlap and only edges, flecks and small stacks should be legible. Coin width is roughly the width of one coin already inside the game chest in reference 2 at equal world scale. Use antique gold, dark ochre shadows and small buttery yellow highlights, no red-orange cast or blown white speculars. Coins stay in coherent clumps so you can visually read the entire stash on a small screen. Keep low hand painted 2:1 isometric geometry, broad shadow planes, clean dark outlining, same upper-left light, simplified mobile Dungeon Empire style. Maintain a wide organic central accumulation with a high mass rear-left, one lesser mass at front-right and a thin irregular scatter along the edge. They touch and make a single communal hoard. Gold sits directly on the floor. No plinth, rug, stones, frame, coffer, or chest. No neat repetitive semicircular domes; the lip of the mound is irregular. The entire sprite is isolated at center with 10% alpha margin and an extremely restrained contact shadow. Leave transparent everywhere else: absolutely no dungeon floor plane, no room, wall, flames, crystal, screen elements, lettering or square backing plate. Output landscape, fully uncut.
